value.content: STATE OF FLORIDA FLORIDA HOUSING FINANCE CORPORATION DEC 29 2025 9:52 AM BENSCHLEY MANOR, LTD., BENSCHLEY MANOR DEVELOPER, LLC, Petitioner, FHFC Case No.: 2025-068BP RFA No.: 2025-205 Application No.: 2026-076BSA vs. FLORIDA HOUSING FINANCE CORPORATION __________________________________________/ FORMAL WRITTEN PROTEST AND PETITION FOR FORMAL ADMINISTRATIVE HEARING Petitioners, Benschley Manor, Ltd., and Benschley Manor Developer, LLC, (collectively, Petitioners or Benschley) by and through undersigned counsel, file this Formal Written Protest and Petition for Formal Administrative Hearing (Petition) pursuant to Sections 120.569 and 120.57(3), Florida Statutes (Fla. Stat.), Chapter 28-106, Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.), and Request for Applications 2025-205 SAIL Financing of Affordable Multifamily Housing Developments to be used in Conjunction with Tax-Exempt Bond Financing and 4% Housing Credits (the RFA). This Petition challenges the intended decision of Respondent, Florida Housing Finance Corporation, (Florida Housing) to award funding in response to the RFA. In support, Petitioners state: Parties 1. Petitioner, Benschley Manor, Ltd., is a Florida limited partnership and the Applicant entity for Application No. 2026-076BSA (Application). For the purposes of this proceeding, Benschley Manor, Ltd.’s address is c/o Manson Bolves Donaldson Tanner, P.A., 109 N. Brush Street, Suite 300, Tampa, Florida 33602. The telephone number is 813-514-4700. 1 2. Petitioner, Benschley Manor Developer, LLC, is a Florida limited liability company, and identified in the Application as the Developer entity as defined by Florida Housing. Rule 67-48.002, F.A.C. For the purposes of this proceeding, Benschley Manor Developer, LLC’s address is c/o Manson Bolves Donaldson Tanner, P.A., 109 N. Brush Street, Suite 300, Tampa, Florida 33602. The telephone number is 813-514-4700. 3. Florida Housing is a public corporation created by Section 420.504, Fla. Stat., and the state agency affected by this Petition. Florida Housing’s address is 227 N. Bronough Street, Suite 5000, Tallahassee, Florida 32301. The telephone number is 850-488-4197. Background and the RFA 4. Florida Housing promotes the public welfare by administering the financing or refinancing of affordable housing and related facilities in the state of Florida. Florida Housing’s statutory authority and mandates are set forth in Part V of Chapter 420, Fla. Stat. 5. Florida Housing is designated as the housing credit agency for the state of Florida in accordance with Section 42(h)(7)(A) of the Internal Revenue Code. §420.5099, Fla. Stat. It has established a competitive solicitation process known as requests for applications to assess the relative merits of proposed affordable housing developments in accordance with Chapters 67-48 and 67-60, F.A.C. 6. On September 29, 2025, Florida Housing issued the RFA seeking applications proposing the development of affordable housing utilizing State Apartment Incentive Loan (SAIL) funding as gap financing, which may be used in conjunction with tax-exempt bond financing or non-competitive housing credits, and, if applicable, home investment partnerships programs. RFA at 2. 2 7. Florida Housing issued a first modification to the RFA on October 27, 2025.1 RFA at 1. 8. The RFA anticipated the award of an estimated $89,650,000 of available SAIL funding appropriated by the Legislature in 2025. RFA at 2. The RFA further identifies that Florida Housing will award a maximum of $33,525,000 of funding for proposed developments with an Elderly Demographic (ALF and Non-ALF) commitment, and $56,125,000 of funding for proposed developments with the Family Demographic commitment. RFA at 2, 104. The RFA sets forth the information required to be provided by an applicant and describes the types of proposed projects that will be eligible for funding. RFA at 1-3. 9. Applicants are required to meet certain mandatory eligibility requirements that must be satisfied in order to be selected for funding. Eligibility items include but are not limited to: disclosure of the Principals for the Applicant and Developer, minimum total proximity scores, demonstration of a Readiness to Process and evidence of site control, and a Development Cost Pro Forma showing sources that equal or exceed uses. RFA at 101-102. All eligibility items are listed within Section Five of the RFA. 10. Certain eligibility requirements have further criteria that are included within the RFA. By example, the RFA requires applicants to identify all Principals of the Applicant, Developer, and all Affiliates of the proposed Development and submit an accurate and complete Principal Disclosure Form. Specifically, an applicant must identify: [T]he Principals of the Applicant and Developer(s) as of the Application Deadline. A Principal Disclosure Form should not include, for any organizational structure, any type of entity that is not specifically included in the Rule definition of Principals. Per subsection 67-48.002(94), F.A.C., any Principal other than a natural 1 All references to “the RFA” and citations within the Petition are to the modified RFA that was issued by Florida Housing on October 17, 2025. 3 person must be a legally formed entity as of the Application Deadline. If the Applicant is requesting 4% Housing Credits, the investor limited partner of an Applicant limited partnership or the investor member of an Applicant limited liability company (or a placeholder for the investor) must be identified on the Principals Disclosure Form. RFA at 14. An applicant will receive 5 points if the uploaded Principal Disclosure Form is stamped “Received” by Florida Housing at least 14 Calendar Days prior to the Application Deadline and stamped “Approved” prior to the Application Deadline. RFA at 15. 11. Rule 67-48.002(94), F.A.C., further identifies what Principals (other than a natural person) must be identified in an applicant’s Principal Disclosure Form as of the Application Deadline. It states: (a) For a corporation, each officer, director, executive director, and shareholder of the corporation; (b) For a limited partnership, each general partner and each limited partner of the limited partnership; (c) For a limited liability company, each manager and each member of the limited liability company; (d) For a trust, each trustee of the trust and all beneficiaries of majority ages (ie.; 18 years of age) as of the Application deadline; (e) For a Public Housing Authority, each officer, director, commissioner, and executive director of the Authority. 12. Additionally, the RFA requires applicants to earn a minimum number of total proximity points to eligible for funding. RFA at 31. Proximity points are based on the distance between the proposed development location and Transit or Community Services. RFA at 30. Applicants may earn proximity points through: (1) qualifying for a specific proximity point boost, (2) providing private transportation or based on the distance between the Development Location Point and Bus or Rail Transit Services, and (3) based on the distance between the Development Location Point and the Community Services. RFA at 31. 4 13. For Community Services, up to 3 Community Services may be selected, for a maximum of 4 proximity points for each service. RFA at 33. Community Services that are available to all Demographics include a Grocery Store, Medical Facility, Pharmacy2, and Public School. Id. 14. The RFA requires Large County3 applicants to earn a minimum of 10.5 total proximity points in order to be eligible for funding. RFA at 31. Large County applicants who earn at least 12.5 proximity points qualify for the Proximity Funding Preference. Id. This preference gives qualified applicants a higher ranking than applicants who do not qualify. RFA at 30. 15.
